newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX probes Yamaichi Singapore deals.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX probes Yamaichi Singapore deals.

text.p: The Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) said on Friday it had launched an investigation into the Singapore operations of Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd.
"We are looking into the matter. It's official," a SIMEX spokeswoman told Reuters.
Yamaichi is embroiled in a corporate racketeering scandal in Tokyo which Japan's Ministry of Finance is investigating.
Tokyo prosecutors have said they suspect Yamaichi of paying 79 million yen (US$669,000) to corporate extortionist Ryuichi Koike. Such payoffs have been banned since 1983.
The Singapore probe was sparked by reports that gains made from SIMEX trades were in part used to make payoffs that are under investigation in Tokyo.
"The Ministry of Finance (in Japan) has an ongoing investigation. Ours is additional," the SIMEX spokeswoman said.
She declined to disclose further details of the probe's scope or the sums under investigation.
Yamaichi in Singapore said it was unaware of any official investigation.
"So far SIMEX has not approached us," a senior Yamaichi manager in Singapore, who declined to be identified, told Reuters.
"The day before yesterday we explained (to SIMEX) that these things happened in Tokyo. So far there has been no further conversation with SIMEX. We are not expecting any," he said.
